messages:
Sam (People Ops): Quick one  an employee is going on unpaid parental leave and asks if they can pause their dependent-care FSA midyear and keep HSA contributions going. Any simple path?

Ari (SWE): Theyll keep employer health coverage but no regular salary during leave. Want to stop DC-FSA deductions (no kidscare paid while on leave) and keep putting $50/mo into HSA if possible.

Jordan (Payroll): Short answer: depends on plan rules. Operationally: 
- FSA (dependent care): most plans lock elections for the plan year unless a qualifying life event occurs; some FSA admins allow a hardship or unpaid leave suspension but thats plan-specific.
- HSA: contributions are tied to HDHP enrollment and payroll deductions; if they remain enrolled in the HDHP and payroll posts taxable wages (even a stipend), payroll can take HSA pre-tax deductions. If no wages, payroll cant pre-tax deduct.

Jordan (Payroll): Practical steps for this employee: 
1) Check SPD/admin rules for DC-FSA midyear suspension or election change (I will ping FSA admin).
2) If FSA change is not allowed, they can: a) stop using FSA funds (can still claim eligible runout if plan allows), or b) enroll in COBRA for FSA only if plan supports it (rare).
3) For HSA: confirm they stay on HDHP. If yes and they want $50/mo from a stipend or residual pay, file a payroll ticket before cutoff to set a one-off deduction code HSA_STIP or change per-pay contribution. If payroll cannot take it, they can make direct post-tax HSA contributions and claim the deduction on Form 8889.

Sam (People Ops): Good. What about vendor minimums or recordkeeper quirks for micro HSA contributions?

Jordan (Payroll): Most recordkeepers accept small amounts; some plans have $25 minimums. Also the HSA custodian may post contributions by calendar date and pro-rate annual limits if you change coverage midyear. Ill confirm our custodian rules and FSA admin suspension policy.

Benefits Bot: Added link: benefits.kb/hsa-fsa-midyear-change and benefits.plan.docs/spd (internal).

Jordan (Payroll): Action items: Ill 1) ping FSA admin about DC-FSA suspension for unpaid leave, 2) confirm HSA custodian acceptance of $50/month micro contributions and any pro-rate implications, 3) post a short KB snippet for people-ops with the decision flow and payroll cutoff timelines. Will tag @Sam when done.

Sam (People Ops): Thanks please include exact payroll ticket wording and cutoff times in the KB so managers can help new parents. :heart:
